title: Preity Zinta Worked 18-Hour Days on Vibe to Get Back to Her Kids in the US
excerpt: The actor addressed Bollywood's work-hours debate at the trailer launch of her upcoming spy comedy, saying her grueling schedule was a personal choice driven by motherhood.
body:
• Preity Zinta revealed she worked 16-18 hour days while filming the spy comedy Vibe, directed by Kunal Kemmu, to finish quickly and return to her children in the United States.
  • Her comments come amid a wider Bollywood debate on work-life balance, sparked by reports that Deepika Padukone exited the film Spirit after seeking an eight-hour workday.
  • Zinta described the shoot as physically demanding, with lengthy action sequences, but said she chose to forgo all social engagements during her 30-40 day stay in India.

Actor Preity Zinta has weighed in on Bollywood's escalating work-hours debate, revealing that she voluntarily worked 18-hour days during the production of her upcoming film Vibe — not because the industry demanded it, but because she wanted to wrap up and fly home to her children.

Speaking at the trailer launch of the Kunal Kemmu-directed spy comedy in Mumbai on September 2, Zinta offered a characteristically direct take. "Each to its own. Of course, I was working for 18 hours because I wanted to finish my work as soon as I can and go back to America to be with my kids," she said. "My focus was, 'I will come, I will finish it, bas mera kaam jaldi khatam kardo.' That was my reason."

The Deepika Padukone Factor

Zinta's remarks land squarely in the middle of a debate that has consumed the Hindi film industry for months. The discussion gained momentum after actor Deepika Padukone reportedly exited Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Spirit over scheduling disagreements. According to industry reports, Padukone — who became a mother in 2024 — had sought an eight-hour workday, a substantial fee and a profit share. The demands reportedly clashed with the director's production plans, leading to her departure from the project.

The episode prompted a broader conversation about whether Bollywood's traditionally demanding schedules are sustainable, particularly for actors balancing parenthood with careers.

A Tough but Deliberate Choice

Zinta, who plays the character Madam H in Vibe, acknowledged that the pace was punishing. Her time in India was limited to roughly 30-40 days, and she said she did not step out for a single evening during the entire shoot. "Every single day I went to shoot, I came back. I didn't even go out for one single day or for even one evening. So, it was a tough shoot," she said.

The film involved significant action sequences that added to the physical toll. "The action was very difficult, I have to say," Zinta noted. "When we shot the action sequences, the hours were very long. I did get kicked, punched, and hit here and there, obviously not on purpose."

Vibe Trailer Debuts

Vibe stars Kunal Kemmu and Sparsh Shrivastava as unlikely heroes in a high-stakes action comedy. The trailer launch also featured Soha Ali Khan, Kemmu's wife, who made a rare public appearance. Kemmu, who also directs the film, previously helmed the 2024 hit Madgaon Express. The film is set to stream on Amazon Prime Video.

Zinta, who has been based in Los Angeles with her husband Gene Goodenough and their twins, has been selective about her Bollywood projects in recent years. Her return to the screen with Vibe marks one of her most prominent roles since her 2018 film Bhaiaji Superhit.
